...RESPONDENTS  (BY SMT MAYA T.R., HCGP)
 This WRIT PETITION is FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227  OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO ISSUE

-2-  NC: 2026:KHC-K:2198  WP No. 201320 of 2023 HC-KAR  A) DIRECT THE RESPONDENT NO.3 TO CONSIDER THE REPRESENTATION DATED 27.03.2023 SUBMITTED BY THE PETITIONER VIDE ANNEXURE-D.
 B) DIRECT THE RESPONDENTS TO NOT LAY / FORM ANY ROAD AND DRAINAGE OVER, THE PETITIONER'S AGRICULTURAL LAND I.E.,

LAND BEARING SY. NO.38/2, MEASURING 01 ACRE 00 GUNTAS,
SITUATED AT KAKKALADODDI VILLAGE OF DEVADURGA TQ: DIST:
RAICHUR, WITHOUT FOLLOWING DUE PROCEDURE ESTABLISHED UNDER LAW.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE SURAJ GOVINDARAJ  ORAL ORDER 1.

Petitioner is before this court seeking for the following reliefs:
a) Direct the respondent No.3 to consider the representation dated 27.03.2023 submitted by the petitioner vide Annexure-D.
b) Direct the respondents to not lay/form any road and drainage over, the petitioner's agricultural land i.e., land bearing Sy.No.38/2, measuring 01 acre 00 guntas, situated at Kakkaladoddi village of Devadurga Tq. Dist.
Raichur, without following due procedure established under law.
c) Such further order other reliefs be granted to the petitioner to which the petitioner would be found entitled to on the facts and circumstances of the case.
Channamma W/O Basavaraj vs The Deputy Commissioner And Ors on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18121507/
2 2.

The grievance of the petitioner is that the respondent authorities, without initiating any acquisition proceedings in accordance with law, have proposed to utilise the land belonging to the petitioner situated in Sy.No.38/2 measuring 1 acre for the purpose of forming a road and a drain.

According to the NC: 2026:KHC-K:2198 HC-KAR petitioner, the said land continues to remain his private property and no proceedings have been initiated either for acquisition or for payment of compensation.

3. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioner fairly submits that the petitioner does not oppose the formation of a road or any other public infrastructure on the said land if the respondents follow the procedure known to law.

The limited grievance of the petitioner is therefore not with regard to the public purpose sought to be achieved, but with regard to the failure of the authorities to initiate lawful acquisition proceedings and compensate the petitioner.

Learned counsel submits that if the respondents initiate appropriate proceedings and determine compensation in accordance with law,
the petitioner would have no objection to the land being utilised for public purposes.

4. This Court has, on numerous occasions, been confronted with matters where lands belonging to private citizens have been utilised by State authorities, including the Public Works Department, the Revenue Department, Panchayat authorities and municipal bodies, for the purpose of formation of NC: 2026:KHC-K:2198 HC-KAR roads, widening of existing roads, or laying of drains and other civic infrastructure, without initiating acquisition proceedings.
These cases are not isolated or stray instances
. On the contrary, this Court has dealt with several such petitions and it appears that this practice is prevalent in several parts of the State.
5. The formation of roads and other infrastructure undoubtedly serves a public purpose.
Development of road infrastructure is essential for mobility of citizens, economic activity, and public welfare.
However laudable the objective sought to be achieved may be, such objective cannot be achieved by disregarding the rights of citizens over their private property.
The rule of law requires that every action of the State must be undertaken strictly in accordance with the procedure established by law.
6. The State possesses the power of eminent domain, which enables it to acquire private property for public purposes.
However, the exercise of such power is subject to strict procedural safeguards prescribed by statute.
The State can deprive a citizen of his property only by resorting to lawful acquisition NC: 2026:KHC-K:2198 HC-KAR proceedings and by payment of just compensation to the landowner.

7. The right to property, though no longer a fundamental right, continues to remain a constitutional right protected under Article 300A of the Constitution of India, which mandates that no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law.

The expression "authority of law"
necessarily implies that the State must act under a valid statutory framework and follow the procedure prescribed therein.

Channamma W/O Basavaraj vs The Deputy Commissioner And Ors on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18121507/
3 8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When private land is utilised for formation of roads or other infrastructure without acquisition proceedings, the citizen is effectively deprived of his property without compensation and without due process of law.

Such action would clearly run contrary to the mandate of Article 300A of the Constitution of India and would undermine the constitutional protection afforded to property rights.
9.

The repeated occurrence of such cases before this Court indicates that the issue may not be confined to a few isolated instances but may represent a systemic administrative practice where road infrastructure has been created on private lands NC: 2026:KHC-K:2198 HC-KAR without acquisition proceedings.
This not only results in violation of constitutional rights of citizens but also exposes the State to repeated litigation and uncertainty.

10. In this background, it becomes necessary that the State Government undertakes a comprehensive and systematic examination of the manner in which lands have been utilised for road infrastructure across the State of Karnataka, so that the rights of citizens are protected and appropriate corrective measures are undertaken wherever necessary.

11. This Court is therefore of the considered opinion that a State-wide audit and verification exercise is required to be undertaken in respect of all roads and related infrastructure within the State so as to ascertain whether the lands utilised for such infrastructure have been obtained through lawful acquisition and whether compensation has been paid to the concerned landowners.

12. The Principal Secretary, Public Works Department, being the administrative authority responsible for the management of State Highways, District Highways and other major road infrastructure in the State, shall initiate and supervise such an exercise.

The said NC:
2026:KHC-K:2198 HC-KAR exercise shall necessarily be undertaken in coordination with the Revenue Department, Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Department, Urban Development Department, municipal corporations, municipal councils, town panchayats, zilla panchayats and gram panchayats, since road infrastructure is managed by multiple authorities at different levels.

13. The exercise to be undertaken by the State shall include identification of all roads within the State, including State Highways, District Roads, Major District Roads, village roads, Panchayat roads, municipal roads and other public roads, and verification of the land records pertaining to such roads.

14. The authorities shall ascertain whether the lands utilised for such roads are Government lands,
lands lawfully acquired under the applicable land acquisition laws, or private lands utilised without acquisition.

In cases where acquisition proceedings have been undertaken, the authorities shall verify the existence of relevant records including acquisition notifications, award proceedings and payment of compensation to the landowners.

NC: 2026:KHC-K:2198 HC-KAR Channamma W/O Basavaraj vs The Deputy Commissioner And Ors on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18121507/
4 15.

entities.text: 2026:KHC-K:2198 HC-KAR Channamma W/O Basavaraj vs The Deputy Commissioner And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In cases where it is found that roads have been formed or widened on private lands without lawful acquisition, the authorities shall identify the extent of land utilised, the identity of the affected landowners, and the department or authority responsible for undertaking such utilisation of land.
16. The authorities shall also ascertain whether compensation has been paid to the affected landowners and, if not, the reasons for the same.

Where such utilisation of land has occurred without acquisition, the State shall prepare a time-bound plan for addressing the grievances of the affected citizens, which may include initiation of acquisition proceedings or any other lawful mechanism recognised under law to ensure that the landowners are paid just and fair compensation.

17. The State Government shall also develop a comprehensive digital database of all roads in the State of Karnataka, indicating the land records relating to such roads, the manner in which such lands were obtained, and the compensation status.

Such a database would ensure transparency,
facilitate better infrastructure planning and enable NC: 2026:KHC-K:2198 HC-KAR identification of instances where corrective measures are required.

18. The State shall also consider establishing an appropriate grievance redressal mechanism enabling citizens to bring to the notice of the authorities instances where their lands have been utilised for public infrastructure without acquisition proceedings.

19. The purpose of directing such an exercise is not merely to address the grievance of the present petitioner but to ensure that systemic corrective measures are undertaken so that citizens are not deprived of their property without lawful acquisition and compensation.

20. Insofar as the present case is concerned, the respondents shall not utilise the land belonging to the petitioner for formation of road or drain unless the land is acquired in accordance with law and compensation is determined and paid to the petitioner, unless the petitioner voluntarily agrees to the utilisation of the land in accordance with law.

21. Hence, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i) The writ petition is allowed.
- 10 - NC: 2026:KHC-K:2198 HC-KAR ii)

Respondents are directed to consider the representation of the petitioner dated 27.03.2023 at Annexure-D.
Channamma W/O Basavaraj vs The Deputy Commissioner And Ors on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18121507/
5 iii) Respondents are restrained from making use of the land of the petitioner for the purpose of widening or laying of any road, without following the due process of law in the manner of acquisition of the property.

iv) Though the above matter is disposed, re-list on 10.04.2026 to enable the Principal Secretary,
Public Works Department to file the affidavit as directed above.

Sd/-
